key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) are local administration-site reactions: nasal discomfort (28% for 70 mg vs 6% placebo), nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, throat irritation, and epistaxis. No SAEs or deaths occurred within 24 hours of etripamil dosing. Serious potential risk is dizziness/syncope due to hypotension and/or bradyarrhythmias/AV block; 0.4% experienced clinically significant hypotension during test dose.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA for etripamil nasal spray. The original NDA (received 3/27/2024) received a Complete Response letter on March 27, 2025, for product-quality/nitrosamine deficiencies and an incomplete facility inspection. The applicant held a Type A meeting on June 4, 2025, and resubmitted a class 2 resubmission on June 13, 2025 (PDUFA goal December 13, 2025), addressing the OPQ deficiencies; with no new deficiencies, the application was approved. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations were applied.

The Applicant had Type A Meeting on June 4, 2025, to discuss issues identified in the March 27, 2025, complete response letter. The Applicant resubmitted their NDA on June 13, 2025.

On June 13, 2025, the Applicant resubmitted NDA 218571. On July 3, 2025, this resubmission was acknowledged as a complete, class 2 resubmission, with the Prescription Drug User Fee Act goal date of December 13, 2025.

The resubmission did not include any new clinical-pharmacology, clinical, or device-related data. OPQ review dated October 23, 2025, recommended approval. Pharmacology-toxicology review discipline also recommended approval. No new deficiencies were identified. Hence, for NDA 218571, the regulatory action for current review cycle is approval.
